title: Choosing the one number a system call declares
summary: A machine specification gives each system call one latency. Fitted on some programs, does it hold for a program it has not seen? A leave-one-program-out test over the corpus, for four ways of choosing the number.
method: For each design and field, the number is fitted on every program but one and judged on the held-out program's operations: an operation that needed more than the number would be late, so its program would not conform.

sections.heading: Where even the worst case of the other programs fails

findings: Even the worst case seen on other programs is not portable for routes on atoms and ions: a new program brings a longer route. A route latency needs a model of distance, or the worst route the layout allows.
Percentiles cover almost every operation but almost never a whole program: one late operation is enough to break a time-triggered schedule.

note: All numbers are measured on QuantumOS's Lean model of RISC-Q control hardware (its cores, hubs and lanes are checked against RISC-Q's RTL cycle for cycle), on generated or published hardware designs. They are properties of that model, not of laboratory hardware.
